objective: Detect and correct access that is no longer appropriate, so that entitlements remain aligned to current role and the principle of least privilege between provisioning events.
description: On a defined cadence, entitlement listings for in-scope systems are extracted from each system of record and reviewed by the accountable owner of that system or by the manager of each user. The reviewer confirms each account remains required at its current privilege level. Items flagged for change are tracked to closure through the ticketing system, and closure is verified against the system before the review is signed off.
owner_role: System owner, with IAM function coordinating

conditions: Users hold persistent entitlements to in-scope systems
not_applicable_when: Access is exclusively just-in-time and ephemeral with no persistent entitlements; the objective is then met by the JIT approval and expiry controls instead

implementation_guidance: Derive the review population by reconciling identity provider, HR system, and each in-scope application, rather than exporting from a single source.
Include service accounts, shared accounts, contractors, and administrative roles; omission of these is the most common scope defect.
Capture reviewer identity, review date, per-entitlement decision, and evidence that revocations actually took effect.
Set cadence from risk, not convenience: privileged access is commonly reviewed more frequently than standard access.
Verify closure against the system rather than accepting the ticket status alone.
design_considerations: Is the reviewer positioned to know whether the access is appropriate?
Does the review cover the full in-scope population, including non-human and privileged accounts?
Does the process define what happens to flagged items, with an accountable owner and a deadline?
operating_considerations: Did every scheduled review occur within its cadence during the period?
Were flagged items actually closed, and how long did closure take?
Can the completeness of each review population be demonstrated?

evidence_examples.note: The review record itself, including population, decisions, and closure.
Identity provider export used to corroborate the completeness of the review population.
Privileged entitlement inventory ensures the privileged population is present in the review.

risks.description: Access accumulates as people change roles, resulting in standing privilege far beyond current need.
Terminated or dormant accounts persist undetected and provide an unmonitored path into the environment.

related_controls.note: Review assumes an authoritative identity population maintained by the identity provider.

source_refs.supports: Identity of the criterion this control is intended to help meet.
Population completeness and closure verification as the dominant points of auditor challenge.
Recommended cadence differentiation by privilege level.

notes: Quarterly cadence is a DriftGuard default, not a SOC 2 requirement. The criteria do not prescribe a review frequency; the organization's own commitments and risk assessment set it.

Primary criterion assignment to CC6.3 reflects the modification-and-removal objective. Access review commonly contributes to CC6.1 and CC6.2 as well; DriftGuard models this via secondary_criteria rather than duplicating the control.
evidence_examples extended to EV-ACCESS-003 in the CC6 phase, so the review's privileged population has a named source.
